notes.meaning: Peter calls himself an apostle, a messenger sent by Jesus with his authority. He writes to believers scattered across five Roman provinces in what is now Turkey. The word "Dispersion" was the name for Jews living away from their homeland. Peter uses it for Christians, both Jewish and Gentile, who are like travelers far from their true home in heaven.

These believers were chosen by God the Father, who knew them beforehand. The Holy Spirit "sanctified" them, which means he set them apart for God and began making them holy. The goal is that they would obey Jesus and be cleansed by his blood. Sprinkled blood recalls the Old Testament sacrifices, where blood was sprinkled on people to apply the sacrifice to them. All three Persons of God work together here, and Peter prays that grace and peace will grow in them more and more.

differ.view: God's "foreknowledge" means his loving choice made beforehand, not merely seeing ahead who would believe. The choice rests on God's free grace alone, and it shows itself in the Spirit's work in us.
"Foreknew" means God set his love on his people before creation. If it only meant God saw that we would believe, our salvation would be taken out of God's hands.

God's real plan is that whoever believes will be saved and whoever endures to the end will be saved forever. Salvation is a free gift, yet promise and duty go hand in hand. Scripture does not teach that God chooses some for heaven apart from this.
God always knew who would respond to his grace, and he chose them to be his children on that basis.

notes.meaning: Peter bursts into praise to God, the Father of Jesus. Out of his great mercy, not because we earned it, God has given us a new birth, a brand-new life from him. That new life brings a "living hope." It is not a wish but a sure hope that keeps us going. It rests on the fact that Jesus rose from the dead.

God's children are also his heirs, so they have an inheritance waiting for them. It can never rot or be destroyed. It can never be spoiled by sin. It never fades like a cut flower. It is kept safe in heaven, out of the reach of thieves and of Satan, for those who belong to Christ.

The inheritance is kept in heaven, and the heirs are guarded on earth. The word for "shielded" is a military word, like soldiers guarding a fort. God's power does the guarding, and faith is the way believers are kept. This protection does not mean no hardship, but it does keep them from final ruin. Full salvation will be shown on the last day, when Christ returns.

differ.view: God's power makes sure that every true believer will keep believing and reach heaven. Our safety rests on God's keeping, not on our own strength.
The heirs are kept "through faith," and faith is how salvation is both received and held on to. Believers are safe as they go on trusting God.
Up to this point Peter describes God's work, and "through faith" is the believer's part in being kept.

notes.meaning: Believers can be full of joy about this hope even while they are sad because of many kinds of trials. Those trials last only a little while, and they come only when God sees they are needed for our good. Fire tests gold and burns away what is impure. In the same way, trials test faith and show it is real. Gold shrinks in the fire, but faith grows stronger. Gold will one day perish, but tested faith will bring praise, glory and honor when Jesus returns.

These readers had never seen Jesus with their eyes, yet they loved him and trusted him. That faith filled them with a joy too big for words, a joy already touched by the glory of heaven. Peter may be remembering Jesus' words to Thomas about those who believe without seeing. They were already receiving what faith aims at, the salvation of their souls. That salvation begins now and will be completed later.

differ.view: The salvation received now is a rescue from all sin into a life of holiness. It prepares for eternal salvation and is a pledge of it.
The soul is saved now by faith, which brings us back into peace with God. This salvation comes by faith in God's promise, not by the merit of our works.

notes.meaning: The Old Testament prophets spoke about this salvation and the grace that would come to believers in Peter's day. They studied it with great care, like miners digging for gold. This shows the gospel is not a new idea, because the prophets pointed to it long ago. It also shows how rich our privilege is, since we see clearly what they longed to understand.

The prophets wanted to know when these things would happen and what those times would be like. The Spirit of Christ was speaking through them, which shows that Christ was alive before he was born as a man. The Spirit told ahead of time about Christ's sufferings and the glories after them: his rising, his going up to heaven, and his coming kingdom. Christ's path shows the pattern for his people too, with suffering first and glory after.

God showed the prophets that their message was mainly for people who would live later, not for themselves. Those things have now been announced by the apostles, through the Holy Spirit sent from heaven at Pentecost. The prophets and the apostles agree because the same Spirit spoke through both. Even angels long to look into these things, like someone bending down to see something more closely.

"Prepare your minds for action" is literally "gird up the loins of your mind." People in long robes tucked them into a belt so they could run, travel or work. Peter means: gather up your thoughts and get ready. Be sober-minded, which means self-controlled and alert. Put your hope fully on the grace God will give when Jesus returns.

Believers are God's children, and children should obey their Father. They should not shape their lives by the wrong desires they followed before they knew God. Conversion makes a person different from what they used to be. The old way of living no longer sets the pattern.

God, who called us, is holy, so his people should be holy in every part of life. Peter quotes Leviticus 11:44, a command first given to Israel, and applies it to Christians. Children should look like their Father. We can never equal God's holiness, but we should keep growing toward it, and God gives the power to obey what he commands.

Believers pray to God as their Father. He is also the Judge, who judges each person's life fairly and has no favorites. So they should live with reverent fear, a deep respect that guards against careless living, not slavish terror. Their time on earth is like a short stay in a foreign land.

To be "redeemed" means to be bought back and set free, as a slave or captive was freed by paying a price. Silver and gold could never pay for a soul, because they perish. The price was the precious blood of Christ, a perfect lamb with no flaw, pictured by the Passover lamb. It freed believers from the empty way of life handed down from their ancestors. Remembering this price is a strong reason to live a holy life.

God planned Christ as the Redeemer before he made the world, so rescue was never an afterthought. In these last times Christ came and was revealed for our sake. Through Christ we trust God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory. So our faith and hope rest in God. Without Christ we could only dread God, but through him we believe, hope and love.

Believers' hearts were made clean when they obeyed the truth of the gospel by believing it. The Holy Spirit did this work in them. It produced sincere love for fellow Christians. Peter urges them to go further and love one another deeply, from a pure heart.

Believers have been born again. This new birth does not come from human parents, which is a birth that ends in death. It comes from God's living word, which never decays. Being born into God's family makes Christians brothers and sisters, which is another reason to love one another. God's word lasts forever, and it keeps working in those who receive it.

Peter quotes Isaiah 40:6-8. People, with all their beauty, strength and riches, are like grass and wildflowers that soon wither and fall. But the word of the Lord stands forever. That same lasting word is the good news that was preached to these readers. Only by receiving it do frail people gain life that lasts.
